prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an outdoor brick-paved courtyard sloping away from the camera wearer toward a building facade and colonnade roughly 8 to 20 metres ahead in the upper-right background, while a child seated in a stroller occupies the lower-right foreground at about 0.5 to 1.0 metre distance. Across the five frames, the camera tilts slightly downward and to the right, bringing more of the stroller and child into view while the camera wearer's left hand holding a small cup enters the bottom-left foreground in frames 4 and 5 at roughly 0.3 to 0.5 metres—well within arm's reach of both the wearer and the child. The map clearly separates the elevated foreground geometry of the child's head, the stroller canopy, and its angled handle struts from the flat ground plane behind them, which is harder to gauge quantitatively from the tilted RGB perspective alone. However, the depth map is somewhat unreliable along the lower-left ground plane where the pavement near the wearer's feet is rendered nearly as bright as the raised hand, and it flattens the child's body and stroller seat into a single smooth surface in the later frames.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the child seated in the stroller in the lower-right foreground (about 0.6 to 1.0 metre from the camera wearer) as a 'person' across all five frames, and adds a second 'person' mask in the bottom-left of frames 4 and 5 for the camera wearer's hand holding a snack cup roughly 0.3 metres from the child. In frames 1 through 3, only the child's head and upper torso are visible at the bottom edge of the frame, whereas by frames 4 and 5 more of the child's torso, arms, and the surrounding stroller at the bottom-right enter the field of view within arm's reach of the wearer's extended left hand. While this map helps distinguish the wearer's reaching hand from the child and background pavement in the final two frames, it is highly unreliable for object classification and boundary accuracy. In frame 1, the 'person' mask spills over to include the blue stroller canopy, in frame 4 the stroller is misclassified as a 'suitcase', in frame 5 the child and stroller are fragmented into multiple overlapping 'person' masks, and distant architectural columns at the top-right (over 10 metres away) are falsely labeled as 'book'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the upper-body and facial keypoints (yellow) and hand keypoints (magenta) of the child seated below and in front of the camera wearer at roughly 0.6 to 1.0 metre distance in the lower-right quadrant. The facial and shoulder landmarks indicate that the child's body is angled toward the bottom-left of the frame, with the head tilted downward and looking toward the child's own lap and the wearer's approaching cup rather than looking up at the camera wearer. Across frames 2 through 5, as the camera view shifts downward to reveal more of the child's upper body, the skeleton captures the child's right hand resting near the chest and left hand reaching toward the right edge of the stroller tray—just 0.2 to 0.3 metres from the wearer's hand—Clarifying limb articulation and head orientation despite heavy cropping and self-occlusion in RGB. However, the pose map is unreliable in frame 1 where it fails to detect the child entirely due to severe occlusion at the bottom border, and in frames 2 through 5 where it completely misses the camera wearer's visible hand in the bottom-left and only intermittently detects the child's magenta hand skeletons (only in frames 2 and 5).
